title: Coherent shifts of products of functors
statement: Let C and D be categories with coherent integer shifts, I an indexing type, and D have I-indexed products. For functors F_i:C→D equipped with CommShift structures, the pointwise product functor P(X)=∏_i F_i(X) has a CommShift structure. Its component P(X[m])→P(X)[m] is the product of the level shift isomorphisms followed by the inverse canonical product-preservation isomorphism of [m]. Its nth projection is pr_n followed by the level shift. The zero and addition laws are those of the given level shifts.

proof.text: Shifts are equivalences and therefore preserve the indexed products. Define the product functor by products on objects and the diagonal product map on morphisms; projection extensionality proves identity and composition.

proof.text: Take the product of the component shift isomorphisms and compose with the inverse canonical product-preservation isomorphism. Composing with a shifted projection gives the corresponding level shift preceded by the projection from the shifted input product.

proof.text: Shifted projections are jointly monic, by composing with the product-preservation isomorphism. Apply them to the proposed naturality square. The projection formula reduces the square to naturality of the given level shift.

proof.text: For zero and addition coherence use the same shifted-projection extensionality. Naturality of the standard zero/addition shift identifications moves them across projections. The remaining equations are precisely the zero/addition equations for each F_i. Package the natural isomorphisms and these laws as CommShift.
